subject: Design review: region-bound retention variants & admin UX
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
Cc: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 20 Apr 2028 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: [Design] Region-bound retention variants & admin UX

Team —

Following up on the Tessera pilot we promised a configurable retention surface that lets admins: (1) pick per-tenant retention presets (P30/P90/Custom), and (2) optionally bind storage region(s) per-tenant or per-workspace. Legal flagged that customer wants both an easy UI and a clear audit trail for where data is stored.

Attached is a lightweight draft (retention-presets-draft.pdf) and a current regional matrix (regional-storage-matrix.xlsx) we pulled from infra. High-level asks:
- Product: propose admin UX that makes binding region obvious and safe (scoping, defaults, warnings).
- Eng: outline constraints for migration vs. on-write routing, and what the minimal MVP is for per-tenant region pins.
- Security/Legal: define required audit events for region changes and deletions.

Can we align on tech approach and a small set of retention presets to ship in Q3? If helpful, I can book a 45m design sync next week.

Thanks —
Jonas
Jonas Weber
Head of Product, Platform
Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>

Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 23 Apr 2028 10:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: [Design] Region-bound retention variants & admin UX

+1 on a short sync. A few immediate thoughts after skimming the draft:

- Preset names should be customer-facing and non-technical (e.g., "Local + 90d", "Global + 1y", "Custom") so that sales/legal can describe them without confusion.
- Need explicit opt-in for region pinning; default should be "regional routing with fallback" to avoid accidental sovereignty promises.
- For Custom, we should require an admin confirmation modal that calls out compliance risk (GDPR, data residency).

Questions for eng: what is the minimum viable surface for admins? Is it: select preset per-tenant + optional per-workspace override? Or do we need per-model pins too?

Irene — will you capture the audit line items we need (change actor, timestamp, old/new region/preset, migration trigger)?

I can gather a short list of customers (Tessera & Acme Analytics) to validate wording if that helps.

Marissa
Senior Product Manager
Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 24 Apr 2028 11:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: [Design] Region-bound retention variants & admin UX

Thanks — technical perspective / constraints:

- Routing vs. Migration: the cheapest MVP is routing on-write based on tenant configuration (write to requested region). Full re-sharding / migrating existing objects between regions is expensive and should be a separate ops feature.
- Backfills: for any existing customer that toggles a new region pin and requests migration, we need a bounded backfill job with per-tenant rate limits and rollback. That adds ~2-4 Sprints depending on infra priorities.
- Metadata + Audit: we can log every change as an audit event (ChangeEvent v1) with actor, ip, timestamp, old/new, and a job-id if a migration is kicked off. No PI in the event payload.
- Admin API: propose endpoints: GET /tenants/{id}/retention, PATCH /tenants/{id}/retention (requires admin role), POST /tenants/{id}/retention/migrate (kick off backfill). Authz caveats apply.

Tradeoffs for UI: if we allow per-workspace overrides, the routing table grows and adds complexity for latency-sensitive workloads. Recommend MVP: tenant-level preset + per-workspace override gated behind feature flag.

I'll slot engineering capacity for a small spike to prove routing on-write next sprint if we agree.

Karthik
Engineering Manager, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

From: Amit Sethi <amit@tessera.ai>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 25 Apr 2028 08:31:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: [Design] Region-bound retention variants & admin UX

Thanks for the thread — Tessera is very interested in a simple admin flow. A couple of asks from our side:

- Can you guarantee that selecting "EU-only" as a preset means the vector DB + KV caches for that tenant are not replicated outside the EU? We need clarity on what "region-bound" entails at the infra layer.
- For Custom retention, can we get an exportable report (CSV/JSON) that shows all objects and their residence as of a point-in-time for audit?

Happy to walk through this on a call. We're available Thursday morning PST.

— Amit
Head of Platform, Tessera AI
amit@tessera.ai

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
Cc: Amit Sethi <amit@tessera.ai>, Rachel - Dataprotec <rachel@dataprotec.com>, legal@acmecorp.com
Date: Wed, 25 Apr 2028 16:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: [Design] Region-bound retention variants & admin UX

Great discussion — summary & next steps: 

Decisions for the MVP:
- Deliver tenant-level retention presets (Local+90d, Global+1y, Custom) with clear customer-facing labels.
- Region binding for new writes (routing-on-write) only; migrations/backfills are opt-in via an ops job (separate ticket INF-8943).
- Admin API as Karthik proposed (GET/PATCH/POST migrate) + audit events (actor, timestamp, old/new, job-id).
- Per-workspace overrides: behind a feature flag for Q4 evaluation.

Action items:
- Marissa: write UX copy for presets and the confirmation modal (due 2028-05-02). Link: https://docs.google.com/document/d/retention-presets-spec
- Karthik: spike routing-on-write and prototype GET/PATCH endpoints (ETA end of sprint 2028-05-16). Create INF-8942 in Jira.
- Irene: enumerate audit events and map to compliance requirements (deliverable 2028-05-06).
- Markus: identify operational runbooks for migration/backfill (RFC INF-8943).

I'll schedule a 30-minute sync with engineering & legal on Thu 2028-04-28 09:00 PT. If anyone objects to the decisions above, flag now; otherwise I'll close this thread and move items into the backlog.

Thanks all —
Jonas
Head of Product, Platform
Redwood Inference
